thread.title: Intraday Update: The Dow Is Up 46 Points. Is All Right With the World Again? - Barron's

author: Brett Arends
title: Intraday Update: The Dow Is Up 46 Points. Is All Right With the World Again? - Barron's
text:
By Brett Arends Updated May 11, 2018 2:09 p.m. ET Hello? Wall Street? Is anybody there?
Illustration: Getty Images The Dow Jones Industrial Average was treading water Friday morning amid thin volumes. Now that halfway decent weather has arrived, everyone who can is apparently taking a personal day. Even the subjects of recent booms were taking an early weekend, as both the bulls and the shorts headed for the golf course. The dollar, oil and long-term interest rates were all becalmed . Apple (AAPL) was off half a percent by lunch, Tesla (TSLA) by 1%.
Overall, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was up a few points and the Standard & Poor's 500 was down a few points.
The good news is that the S&P 500, after this week's surge, is finally back in positive territory for the year.
Does this mean anything much? Quite possibly , argues LPL Financial. Going back to 1970, they calculate, whenever the S&P 500 has been in the black by May it has almost always ended up positive for the year overall: This has happened 35 out of 36 times, they say.
Fascinating reading—subject, of course, to the iron law of financial forecasts, which is that they all have a roughly 50% chance of being correct this time around. Alternatively, you can sell in May and go away .
LPL also noted that small-caps, as measured by the S&P 600 index, just hit a new all-time high. As small companies are generally more levered to the domestic economy, and demand for their stocks is generally more levered to the mood on Wall Street, this is all very cheerful.
Oh, and the Atlanta and New York Feds, in their competing “NowCasting” models, argue second-quarter gross domestic product is on track for healthy growth between 3% ( New York ) and even 4% ( Atlanta ).
So God is in his heaven, and all is right with the world? Sure, why not?
If only this weren’t already reflected in valuations.
Or, as someone wise once said: "There is no such thing as a risk-free investment—only an investment whose risks are not yet apparent."
S&P 500 : Little changed at 2724.17
Dow 30 : +46.28 points, or 0.2%, at 24785.81
Nasdaq : -0.2% to 7387.98
Vix : +0.8% to 13.33
10-year Treasury Yield : 2.97%
Midday Movers MGM Resorts International (MGM) has declined nearly 5% following its investor day. The casino operator announced a $2 billion share repurchase program , which represents about 35%-to-45% of free cash flow generated through the end of 2020, according to Jefferies analyst David Katz. MGM also issued revenue guidance of some $14 billion in 2020. While it was in line with the growth trajectory Jefferies expected, investors clearly weren't impressed.
Illustration: Getty Images PPG Industries (PPG) slipped more than 2.5% after the company fired its controller for a million-dollar oops in accounting . PPG said in a statement: “The investigation has found evidence that the improper accounting entries were made by certain employees at the direction of the company’s former vice president and controller.”
Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (RARE) has popped 3.7% after Barclays upgraded the stock to Overweight from Equal Weight. "Following Crysvita approval in X-linked hypophosphatemia in the US and the announcement of a higher than expected price, we see meaningful upside to our previous revenue assumption," writes analyst Gena Wang.
Nektar Therapeutics (NKTR), one of the most volatile stocks in the S&P 500 , has risen 1.1% after consensus-beating sales trumped a larger-than-expected loss .
TechnipFMC (FTI) has gained 1.7% after DNB Markets upgraded it to Buy from Hold. — Crystal Kim
